<thought>After checking commercial availability, 2‑methylcyclohexanol is not listed as buyable, but 2‑methylcyclohexanone is a common reagent and is commercially available. We can obtain the required cyclohexanol fragment by (1) methylating cyclohexanone to give 2‑methyl‑cyclohexanone (already buyable, so we can use it directly), (2) reducing the ketone to the corresponding alcohol, and (3) performing the ether formation with 5‑bromo‑2,4‑pentadien‑1‑ol followed by esterification with penta‑2,4‑dienoic acid. This gives a 4‑step synthesis (well under the 5‑step limit) and all leaf compounds are commercially available and inexpensive.</thought>
